articles.title: Champagne Vortex
articles.summary: Tight concentric swirl of violet, magenta and pink with a dense glittery texture, like a hypnotic vortex. Reads as a purple-blue field with a big pink-orange pinwheel in the middle; the speckle dots turn into a fine glitter haze.
articles.what: Champagne Vortex gradient blend Up close: One big three-armed swirl: a champagne-grey grainy core, then orange-peach, hot magenta and blue-violet arms, fading to flat blue-violet at the edges. Hundreds of tiny ring dots with dark centres are sprinkled across it, and the core has a fine grain. The swirl fills about the whole 512 px tile. From a distance: Reads as a purple-blue field with a big pink-orange pinwheel in the middle; the speckle dots turn into a fine glitter haze. Measured spec (average): metal 116, roughness 117, coat 123. Shine: satin. Metal: medium. It brings its own colours.
when: Best on: hood, roof, hero panel.
Fits: show car, open wheel, gt / sports car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Champagne Vortex" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Single large motif: one swirl per tile, centre of the tile at its middle; put it on the hood or a wide side panel so the whole spiral shows
Small parts only get a slice of the colour ramp
Numbers fight the swirl; use a solid black or white plate or fat outlined digits.
None: the swirl is the whole design, anything on top is noise
Pairs well with: black, chrome, hot pink, white.
pitfalls: Not concentric rings as the old card says: arms spiral in a pinwheel
Not a smooth gradient: it has grain and hundreds of ring dots
Avoid: numbers over the swirl centre, next to other busy patterns.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 116 (pearl-level metal), roughness 117 (satin or eggshell), clearcoat 123 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: numbers over the swirl centre, next to other busy patterns.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: none: the swirl is the whole design, anything on top is noise; a plain black or white plate for numbers is the only thing worth adding
Patterns to avoid: dots, circles or stripes: add clutter to an already speckled swirl; carbon or camo: mud against the colour ramp
Spec overlays that work: gloss clear band: a smooth shiny strip against the speckle; none else: spec already swings widely
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
